description: Why is immigration one of the most fiercely debated topics in American life, and how do policies dictate who gets to belong? In this Writing and Rhetoric course, we will explore US immigration to understand how policy shapes national conversations and the lived experiences of immigrant families. Through historical texts, literature, and personal narratives, we will examine how factors such as race, gender, and religion impact the immigrant journey and redefine American identity. Along the way, you will sharpen your critical reading, writing, and discussion skills to cut through the political noise and articulate your own informed voice. This course will include group discussions, a visit to a campus immigration archive, and in-class investigations of policies and immigrant narratives. As you draft and revise your work, these activities will build toward a research-driven ArcGIS Story Map on a migration topic of your choice. You will wrap up the course by reflecting on your progress as a writer and how you will carry these tools into future college courses.
